title: .agents/compatibility.json
description: The machine-readable declaration of a repository's agent-context layout. It is read by agentkit and the hooks, not loaded into model context. `agentkit verify` checks declared paths and settings against the filesystem.

policyDraft.description: Output of `agentkit policy scaffold`. Entries are not enforced until a human reviews and promotes them into `policy`.

agentkitVersion.description: Version of the kit vendored into this repo. Drives the cross-repo drift check.

canonical.description: Every path the verifier asserts exists. Paths are repo-relative and POSIX-separated.

optionalFiles.description: Canonical files that are optional for repositories where they do not apply, such as `obligations.md`.

adapters.description: Every harness reach path. The verifier checks native Codex discovery, exact import lines, and relative symlinks against their declared targets; manual imports remain explicitly unmeasured.

enforcement.description: Per-harness enforcement level. `blocking` is a claim that a deny actually denies, and a provider-backed live self-test is what makes the claim honest. Unknown providers may be declared, but self-test refuses their blocking claim until a provider-specific probe exists.

enforcementEvidence.description: Latest provider-specific live deny-and-observe result. `agentkit self-test` rewrites one snapshot per harness; the verifier invalidates it when the installed adapter bytes change.

autoMemory.description: Declared state of Claude Code auto memory. Asserted against settings.json `autoMemoryEnabled`; a mismatch is an error. RepoCharter defaults to `off` because durable context belongs in reviewed, portable project files. `on` is an explicit Claude-only exception and requires autoMemoryReason.

autoMemoryReason.description: Required when autoMemory is `on`. Explain why this repository accepts machine-local, unreviewed, Claude-only startup context instead of the canonical project-memory system.

budgets.description: Context-budget constants used by the verifier and their documented sources.

codexProjectDocMaxBytes.description: HARD FAIL threshold for the Codex-visible chain. The real shipped default, not a fraction of it: gating below what is enforced buys nothing and costs real deletions from a safety file.

codexBudgetSource.description: Where the constant was read, with a commit SHA and a date. If this is stale, re-read before trusting the number.

claudeLineTarget.description: WARN threshold on the Claude-visible repo-controlled set. Anthropic publishes no byte cap, only an adherence target, and a qualitative target earns a warning rather than a build failure.

policy.description: What the mechanical gates enforce. Read at runtime by the Edit/Write and MCP hooks, and compiled into settings.json permissions.deny by `agentkit apply`. Anthropic's steer is followed here: hard tool/path blocks go to permissions.deny, and hooks carry only what permissions cannot express.

protectedBranches.description: Push to these asks; force-push to these is denied.

denyBashPatterns.description: Repository-specific Bash denials read at runtime by the Bash gate. `agentkit policy scaffold` can import candidates from a supported legacy shell gate.

askBashPatterns.description: Same shape as denyBashPatterns. Claude prompts directly. In approval-capable Codex turns, the adapter hands confirmation to Codex's native permission flow; with approvals disabled, it denies. PreToolUse cannot itself force a Codex prompt, so the agent must submit the call for native approval.

reason.description: Shown to the agent on denial. A gate that explains itself is one people fix rather than route around.

denyWritePaths.description: Paths no agent may Edit or Write. Compiled into permissions.deny AND checked by the hook, deliberately twice: permissions.deny is the client-enforced layer, the hook is what still fires if a settings layer is missing.

pattern.description: Python regex matched against the full tool name, e.g. ^mcp__.*__deploy_to_vercel$

whenArgMatches.description: Optional narrowing: deny only when a named argument matches a regex. Lets `deploy(target=preview)` through while denying `deploy(target=production)`.

measureOnWrite.description: Measurements to report before and after edits to matching paths. Each entry names a path glob, measurement type, and reason.

scripts.description: Unicode script names for `script-lengths`, for example ["Cyrillic"]. Counts are reported separately for each configured script.

validation.description: Provider-neutral clean-code commands run by `agentkit verify`, and therefore by the installed pre-commit hook. Commands are argv arrays rather than shell strings so quoting cannot change what executes.

fallbacks.description: Documented behavior when a harness lacks a feature assumed by the canonical layout. Naming the fallback keeps provider-specific gaps explicit.

examples.missingPlanMode: Use the active conversation plus docs/project/PLAN.md

retiredPaths.description: Globs for retired content that remains checked in, such as fallback mirrors or archived versions. `agentkit apply` adds these paths to the agnix exclude list.

harnessWritten.description: Glob allowlist of paths created by the harness and accepted by the verifier. Claude Code can create skill directories under .claude/skills, including verify/ and run-<name>/.

exceptions.description: Documented per-repository deviations that the verifier and future maintainers can inspect.

rule.description: Which design rule is being departed from.

pattern.description: One POSIX ERE matched against the command with grep -E.

allOf.description: A conjunction harvested from chained gate conditions; every pattern must match.

reason.description: Shown on denial. A gate that explains itself is one people fix rather than route around.

_repaired.description: Legacy repair provenance retained for declarations already emitted by agentkit 0.2.x.

enforcementLevel.description: blocking = a deny is mechanically refused and a provider-specific live self-test proves the installed wire path. advisory = the harness reads the rules or has untrusted hooks but nothing proven stops it. none = the harness does not participate.
